content:
Rumors suggest Apple's iPhone lineup this fall will center around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Below are the three most important feature differences—apart from price—that may influence your upgrade decision.

Form factor: Traditional vs. foldable

This is the most obvious difference, but it's still worth highlighting because it's also the most crucial distinction.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the fundamental design that iPhones have used for years. Reportedly, their screen sizes and overall design will be identical to the previous generation. If you prefer the traditional iPhone feel, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. Its form factor is completely different—featuring an outer screen that's shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and an inner screen resembling an iPad mini.

Cameras: The Pro lineup will continue to lead

Apple has consistently placed its most advanced and innovative camera technology in the Pro lineup. This year will be no different.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature roughly the same camera capabilities as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: it won't include a telephoto lens.

Reports indicate the iPhone Ultra will still carry the same main lens, ultrawide lens, and front-facing camera as the Pro lineup. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro series, and its performance is rumored to be even better this year.

Performance: Both will run on the A20 Pro chip, but materials affect real-world performance

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to be powered by the A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, their performance levels may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will retain the same all-aluminum unibody design as the iPhone 17 Pro, also equipped with a vapor chamber for cooling. These two changes made the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance notably better than its predecessor, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures when handling demanding tasks.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a lightweight titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, though only one leaker has mentioned this so far. Due to the material differences, even with the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Ultra may fall slightly short in performance under direct sunlight or during intensive tasks.
